# createPerson — POST /people/create

Create a person without matching

## Verified behaviors

- **A plausible vanId is echoed back as matched, existent or not** — The vanId in the body is never checked against the database: any id in the range this database has ever assigned answers 302 Matched with the id echoed straight back, even when it names no one — the Location it points at answers 404. Nothing is created. ([replay](../behaviors/create-echoes-a-plausible-vanid-blindly.md))
- **An identical payload creates a second person record** — No de-duplication happens: posting a payload identical to an existing person's — same name, same email — returns 201 with a fresh vanId, and both person records now exist. ([replay](../behaviors/create-never-deduplicates.md))
- **A vanId that exists matches instead of creating** — When the body carries a vanId that exists, nothing is created: the answer is the same 302 match stub findOrCreate gives, with a Location pointing at the existing person. ([replay](../behaviors/create-with-a-vanid-matches-instead.md))
- **An implausible vanId hides a create behind the 302** — A vanId outside the range the database has ever assigned is ignored — but the request is not refused: the rest of the payload is stored as a new person record, and the answer is still the 302 Matched stub, pointing at the person just created. Only the unfamiliar vanId in the response betrays that something was written. ([replay](../behaviors/create-with-an-implausible-vanid-creates-anyway.md))
- **An empty body creates a blank person record** — Every field is optional, including the name, so `{}` is a valid payload on both create endpoints: create answers 201 Stored, and findOrCreate — with no criteria to match on — answers 201 UnmatchedStored. Each call leaves a nameless person record behind. ([replay](../behaviors/empty-bodies-create-blank-people.md))

## Behavior

Stores the payload as a new person record. **No de-duplication happens**: posting a name and email identical to an existing person's creates a second person record. Use POST /people/findOrCreate when you want matching — bearing in mind that it too creates a second person record unless your payload reaches the minimum match combination documented there (name alone never does).

Outcomes:

- **The body supplies a `vanId` that exists** — nothing is created and that person is returned as **302 Found**, exactly as findOrCreate would answer.
- **The body supplies a plausible `vanId` that matches nothing** — still **302 Found**, echoing the id straight back. The id is never checked against the database: anything from 100000000 (where this database's ids start) up through the newest id ever assigned answers `{"vanId": <as sent>, "status": "Matched"}`, with a `Location` that then answers 404. Nothing is created. This case has also been seen to answer **404** directly instead — rarely; see that response below.
- **The body supplies an implausible `vanId`** (below 100000000, negative, or beyond the newest assigned id) — the id is ignored, but the request is not refused: the rest of the payload **is stored as a new person record**, and the answer is still **302 Found** with `"status": "Matched"` and a `Location` pointing at the person just created — not a 201. The status code cannot tell you whether a create happened; a `vanId` in the response you never sent can.
- **The body supplies `"vanId": 0`** — the id is ignored entirely and the ordinary create runs: **201 Created**, as if the field were absent.
- **Anything else** — **201 Created** with `{"vanId": …, "status": "Stored"}`. A payload identical to an existing person is not a special case: it creates a duplicate.
- **The body is empty (`{}`)** — every field is optional, so this too returns **201**, creating a blank person record with no name.

## Example

```bash
curl -sS -X POST \
  'https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/create' \
  -u "app-name:$NGP_API_KEY|1" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
  "firstName": "Cre",
  "lastName": "Atetest"
}'
```

## Responses

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | Never sent by this endpoint. This is where a redirect-following client *lands* when the body carried a `vanId` that already exists: ``` POST /people/create {"vanId": 102714558, …} ← 302 Found Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/102714558 {"vanId": 102714558, "status": "Matched"} GET /people/102714558 ← client re-issues the request at Location ← 200 OK { full person record — the body documented here } ``` So on the vanId path your code sees this 200 and a full `Person` — and, critically, a response that looks nothing like the 201 you get when a person record really was created. Check `resp.history` / `resp.redirected`, or just don't send a `vanId` to a create endpoint. And when the echoed `vanId` names no person — see the outcomes above — the redirect-following client lands on a **404** here instead of this 200. See POST /people/find for the full redirect-following notes, including the `curl -X POST -L` gotcha. | [Person](../schemas/Person.md) |
| `201` | A new person record was created. No `Location` header is sent — the new id is in the body. | `PersonStored` |
| `302` | The body carried a `vanId`, and nothing else in the payload was considered. Sent whether or not that id exists — a plausible id is a genuine match or a blind echo whose `Location` answers 404, and an implausible one quietly hides a create, with the new person's id (not the one sent) in the body. See the outcomes above. | `PersonMatched` |
| `400` | Validation error, as the standard JSON envelope. ([details](../ERRORS.md#badrequest)) | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) |
| `401` | Missing/invalid API key, or a database mode the key does not have access to. ([details](../ERRORS.md#unauthorized)) | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) |
| `404` | A body `vanId` that matches no person has been seen to answer this way — the standard error envelope, nothing created — in place of the blind 302 echo the identical request normally gets. Rare and not reproducible on demand; code that sends a `vanId` here should treat a 404 as possible. | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded. ([details](../ERRORS.md#toomanyrequests)) | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) |
| `500` | Internal server error. ([details](../ERRORS.md#servererror)) | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) or [AspNetError](../ERRORS.md#aspneterror) |

### `201` body — PersonStored

### `302` body — PersonMatched

An existing person was found and nothing was written. The only match-stub shape that accompanies a 302: from find, findOrCreate, create when the body's vanId exists, and update.
